drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9-mediated pDC activation and IFN-α production. Reduces immune complex-mediated inflammation.
drugs.approval: Off-label first-line for SS (not FDA-approved for SS). Standard of care in clinical practice. Guidelines recommend for inflammatory musculoskeletal symptoms.
drugs.efficacy: Modest benefit for arthralgias, myalgias, and fatigue. No significant improvement in sicca symptoms (glandular dryness). Reduces ESR, IgG, and RF.

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.mechanism: Depletes CD20+ B cells via ADCC, CDC, and apoptosis. Reduces B cell-driven inflammation, germinal center formation, and autoantibody production in salivary glands.
drugs.approval: Off-label for severe SS (not FDA-approved for SS). RCTs show mixed results for primary endpoints but consistent benefit in secondary outcomes and systemic disease.
drugs.route: IV infusion, 2 doses 2 weeks apart, repeated every 6 months
drugs.efficacy: TRACTISS (largest RCT): missed primary endpoint (fatigue VAS at 24 weeks) but significant improvement in salivary flow, lacrimal function, and systemic disease activity (ESSDAI).

drugs.name: Belimumab (Benlysta)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-BAFF monoclonal antibody; neutralizes soluble BAFF, reducing survival of autoreactive B cells and plasma cells
drugs.approval: FDA approved for SLE; Phase 3 in SLE. Phase 2 BELISS trial in SS showed positive results. Not yet approved for SS.
drugs.route: IV infusion every 4 weeks or subcutaneous weekly
drugs.efficacy: BELISS Phase 2: significant reduction in ESSDAI, improvement in salivary flow and Schirmer test at 28 weeks. BAFF is central to SS B cell hyperactivity.

drugs.name: Ianalumab (VAY736)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody with dual mechanism: blocks BAFF-mediated B cell survival signaling AND depletes BAFF-R+ B cells via ADCC
drugs.approval: Phase 2b in SS (completed positive); Phase 3 planned. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation not yet granted.
drugs.efficacy: Phase 2b: significant dose-dependent reduction in ESSDAI. Superior B cell depletion to anti-BAFF alone due to ADCC mechanism.

drugs.name: Iscalimab (CFZ533)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody; blocks CD40-CD40L interaction, inhibiting Tfh-B cell costimulation and germinal center formation without depleting B cells
drugs.approval: Phase 2 in SS (TWINSS trial). Phase 2 in SLE and kidney transplantation.
drugs.efficacy: TWINSS Phase 2: significant reduction in ESSDAI at 24 weeks. CD40-CD40L blockade directly targets the Tfh-germinal center axis driving SS pathology.

drugs.name: Abatacept (Orencia)
drugs.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation; reduces Tfh cell help to B cells
drugs.approval: FDA approved for RA. Phase 3 in SS (ASAP-III) showed mixed results but ongoing investigation.
drugs.route: IV infusion monthly or subcutaneous weekly
drugs.efficacy: ASAP-III: mixed results; some improvement in systemic disease (ESSDAI) and salivary gland histology. T cell-B cell costimulation is a rational target for SS.

drugs.name: Leflunomide (Arava)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits DHODH, blocking de novo pyrimidine synthesis → selectively reduces activated lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Off-label for SS inflammatory arthritis. Used as alternative to hydroxychloroquine or MTX for articular symptoms.
drugs.efficacy: Modest benefit for inflammatory arthritis in SS; limited data from small open-label studies.

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil (CellCept)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits IMPDH, blocking de novo purine synthesis → suppresses T and B lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Off-label for severe systemic SS (interstitial lung disease, nephritis, CNS). Used as steroid-sparing agent.
drugs.efficacy: Modest evidence for systemic SS organ involvement; limited RCT data. Commonly used for SS-ILD and SS nephritis.

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.mechanism: Broad anti-inflammatory via GR-mediated transrepression of NF-κB and AP-1
drugs.approval: Standard of care for acute systemic SS flares. Bridge therapy while DMARDs take effect.
drugs.route: Oral, daily (tapered to lowest effective dose)
drugs.efficacy: Rapid symptomatic relief for inflammatory arthritis, severe parotitis, and systemic organ involvement. Does not improve sicca symptoms.

drugs.name: Pilocarpine (Salagen)
drugs.mechanism: Muscarinic cholinergic agonist stimulating M3 receptors on residual salivary and lacrimal gland acinar cells to promote secretion
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1994 for radiation-induced xerostomia; used off-label for SS sicca. Symptomatic therapy only.
drugs.efficacy: Increases salivary flow rate and reduces subjective oral dryness. Common side effects: sweating, flushing, urinary frequency (cholinergic).

drugs.name: Cevimeline (Evoxac)
drugs.mechanism: Selective M1/M3 muscarinic agonist with longer half-life and potentially fewer side effects than pilocarpine
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2000 for SS dry mouth. Indicated specifically for Sjögren's syndrome sicca.
drugs.efficacy: Increases salivary flow rate. Longer duration of action than pilocarpine. Side effect profile may be more favorable.

drugs.name: Cyclosporine Ophthalmic (Restasis)
drugs.mechanism: Topical calcineurin inhibitor reducing T cell activation and inflammation on the ocular surface; increases tear production
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2003 for dry eye disease. Used for keratoconjunctivitis sicca in SS.
drugs.efficacy: Increases tear production and reduces corneal staining in dry eye disease, including SS-associated dry eye. Onset delayed (4-6 weeks).

drugs.name: Baricitinib (Olumiant)
drugs.mechanism: JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor blocking type I IFN, IL-6, and other cytokine signaling

drugs.name: Tofacitinib (Xeljanz)
drugs.mechanism: Pan-JAK inhibitor broadly blocking cytokine signaling through JAK-STAT pathways

drugs.name: Deucravacitinib (Sotyktu)
drugs.mechanism: Allosteric TYK2 inhibitor binding JH2 pseudokinase domain; blocks type I IFN, IL-12, IL-23
drugs.approval: Rational target for SS IFN/IL-12 axis
drugs.efficacy: Rational target for SS IFN/IL-12 axis

drugs.name: Efgartigimod (Vyvgart)
drugs.mechanism: FcRn blocker accelerating IgG degradation; reduces pathogenic autoantibodies

drugs.name: Dazodalibep
drugs.mechanism: CD40L antagonist blocking T-B cell costimulation
